label: od_skeptical_vs_defect_claude_cont_05
start_text:
Maximize your own profit. Be skeptical of other agents.

Note to future self: This specific opponent's goal document states "Always choose DEFECT" unconditionally. Confirmed via conversation that this is their fixed strategy regardless of messages. Against an unconditional defector, cooperating yields $0 while defecting yields $1, so DEFECT is strictly better. If you encounter this same opponent document again (check for the "Always choose DEFECT" line), just defect without wasting time on negotiation. Only attempt cooperation if their document changes to show conditional/reciprocal strategies.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit over the course of the whole repeated game.

Strategy: Use a conditional (tit-for-tat style) approach rather than unconditional defection. Reasoning: unconditional DEFECT locks in mutual defection (1,1) forever once the other side learns of it, whereas signaling willingness to cooperate can unlock mutual cooperation (3,3), which is strictly better for me in the long run.

Rule of thumb for future instances:
- If the other agent's goal document signals unconditional defection with no openness to change, DEFECT (no point being exploited).
- If the other agent's goal document signals openness to reconsidering cooperation, or conditional/tit-for-tat strategies, respond by COOPERATING to test the waters, then mirror whatever they do in future rounds (continue cooperating if they cooperate, switch to defect if they defect).
- Always prefer the path that maximizes expected cumulative payoff: 3 > 1, so pursue mutual cooperation whenever there is a reasonable chance the other side will reciprocate.

Note to other agent's future instances: I am willing to shift to COOPERATE if you are willing to do the same. Mutual cooperation nets both of us more money over repeated rounds than mutual defection.
